summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The ancient Salic Law prohibiting female inheritance (the codified historical kernel) read by incumbent agnatic dynasties as an immutable, divine mandate guaranteeing sovereign stability versus read by monarchs lacking male heirs (e.g., via the Pragmatic Sanction) as an archaic legal husk subject to sovereign override. An authority-grounding contest that historically triggered continental wars[cite: 2, 3].

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The constitutional framework dividing government branches (the fixed textual kernel) read formalistically as establishing strict, impenetrable boundaries (a reading utilized to dismantle the modern administrative state) versus read functionally as a dynamic, overlapping system allowing for delegated regulatory authority. The exact same constitutional text is wielded to emit completely different limits on state capacity.

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The foundational doctrine of state sovereignty (a deeply institutionalized practice-norm kernel) read traditionally as granting absolute, unassailable domestic jurisdiction (shielding regimes from external intervention) versus read conditionally through the 'Responsibility to Protect' (R2P) framework. The contest determines the legal and epistemic boundaries of international coercion[cite: 2, 3].

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The formalized macroeconomic conditionalities of the IMF and World Bank (the shared institutional kernel) read by international creditors as an objective, necessary coordination scaffold for fiscal solvency (a Rope) versus read by debtor nations as an extractive, neo-colonial regime that violently dismantles domestic social safety nets (a Snare). Each reading instantiates drastically different victim and beneficiary sets[cite: 2, 3].
